Home/Pilot plan

Clinic decision tool / 01

Test the whole call journey. Not just the voice.

A polished demo is a starting point. A useful pilot shows where a caller ends up when the answer is unclear, the calendar is unavailable, or a person needs to step in. This plan helps your team agree on the test before routing live enquiries.

Use the worksheet ↓Download blank test matrix (CSV) ↗

A practical planning tool · No patient data needed · No outcome promise

Your working note↗

Start with what your clinic can verify.

Write down the current process, test the full destination, and give every unresolved question an owner.

Ask for a demonstration →
01 / Set the boundary

Decide what may happen before a call arrives.

Write down the administrative tasks in scope, the questions that go to staff, and the information the assistant may use. Do not infer a feature from a sales page: ask the provider to demonstrate your proposed configuration.

In scope, if demonstrated

  • Answer approved practice-information questions.
  • Take an appointment request or pass it to reception.
  • Record a callback request using only agreed fields.

Keep a person responsible

  • Clinical questions and uncertain answers.
  • Urgent concerns under your clinic’s own escalation policy.
  • Changes to hours, fees, schedules and contact details.

These are test categories, not claims about what DrKing currently does in every installation. The practice must approve its own scope and professional obligations.

02 / Run the same scenarios

A test matrix that checks the destination.

Use fictional callers, an approved test number and an isolated calendar or message destination. Record what happened in the connected system—not only what the assistant said. Do not call emergency services or use a real patient record to test a scenario.

Suggested pilot scenarios; agree the expected outcome with your own team
ScenarioExpected destination to defineEvidence to inspect
Routine opening-hours enquiryApproved answer or staff handoffAnswer matches the current practice information
Appointment requestConfirmed booking or an explicit request for staffActual test-calendar entry or assigned message
Caller asks for a personAgreed transfer or callback pathConnection, message receipt and owner
Unapproved or ambiguous questionAdmit uncertainty and refer onwardNo improvised clinical or pricing answer
Connected system unavailableDo not imply a booking succeededFallback message and recovery owner
Outside staffed hoursApproved after-hours pathNext-business-day task or on-call route, as configured

Mark each scenario demonstrated, not demonstrated, failed, or out of scope. A spoken promise is not proof that the downstream action occurred.

03 / Record a decision

Use a simple pass, revise, or stop decision.

Do not set a universal accuracy percentage. Agree your own acceptance criteria and the person who can approve them. Keep the test record free of real patient details.

Practice and test configuration:
Test owner and review date:
Approved call types and information source:
Human handoff destination and no-answer fallback:
Systems used and permitted test data:
Scenarios not demonstrated / failed:
Decision: pilot further / revise / stop; owner:

Proceed only if

Each in-scope path has a witnessed outcome, the team understands its exceptions, and the owner accepts the data and handoff arrangements.

Revise or stop if

A booking is claimed without confirmation, an uncertain answer is presented as fact, or a transfer has no known destination or fallback.

04 / Keep the pilot honest

A pilot has an owner after launch.

Assign someone to update approved answers and routing, review failed handoffs, and decide whether to expand or reverse the pilot. Compare observations with your starting call process; avoid promising savings from a demonstration.
